Deployment

The Acme server is a single static binary that listens on one port and writes structured logs to standard output. It expects to run behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS, and it expects to be restarted rather than reconfigured when its settings change.

Behind a reverse proxy

Forward the original client address in the X-Forwarded-For header and the original scheme in X-Forwarded-Proto. Without those two headers the server logs the proxy's address for every request and generates absolute URLs with the wrong scheme.

location / {
  proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

Zero-downtime restarts

On SIGTERM the server stops accepting new connections, finishes the requests already in flight, and exits once the last one completes or after the shutdown grace period elapses, whichever comes first. Set the proxy's own timeout above that grace period so a draining request is never cut off by the layer in front of it.

SignalEffect
SIGTERMGraceful drain, then exit.
SIGINTIdentical to SIGTERM.
SIGKILLImmediate termination; in-flight requests are lost.

The monitoring guide describes the health endpoint a proxy should poll to decide when a freshly started instance is ready to receive traffic.
